text: Registered primary hypothesis H1 (AdamW decay 0.01 improves test accuracy over decay 0) is not supported. The mean paired accuracy difference is zero, and the paired bootstrap interval is degenerate at [0, 0] because regularized and unregularized arms make identical argmax predictions on all 360 test examples for seeds 0-2. The registered falsification rule (interval wholly below zero) is not triggered, and the directional support rule (interval wholly above zero) is not met. Predictions P1 (|mean delta| <= 1 pp) and P2 (interval includes zero) hold; P3 (interval wholly above zero) is not observed.
limitations: Zero discordant pairs carry no sign information, so this shows that the registered intervention did not flip any test prediction at this budget. It does not show that decay is equivalent to no decay. Only decay 0.01, learning rate 0.001, 850 steps, three seeds and one random split were tested. The bootstrap conditions on the trained models and does not capture training-seed variance.

text: The registered arms have different loss histories for each seed, consistent with the intervention changing training. The observed seed spread falls within the preregistered range. These checks do not independently prove that the entire optimizer implementation is correct; numerical values are regenerated in the result tables.
limitations: P7 sits at the registered lower bound, and three seeds estimate seed variance poorly. P8 shows that decay changes training, not that the implementation matches the update rule; that is checked separately by the zero-gradient unit test (E8) and the mechanism analysis (E5).

text: The sensitivity arm (decay 0.001) makes test predictions identical to the unregularized arm on all seeds, so the accuracy result is null for both non-zero decay values tested.
limitations: Descriptive comparison, not a registered primary endpoint. Both non-zero values share the same learning rate and 850-step budget. Nothing is claimed about larger decay or longer training.

text: The logistic regression baseline reaches test accuracy slightly below the MLP arms, and the class-prior floor sits at chance. The task is learnable by a linear model at roughly the same level, so the MLP is not operating at a trivial level.
limitations: The logistic baseline has one seed and was not tuned under a separate protocol. Its L2 penalty is sklearn's default, not the registered decay. The difference from the MLP is descriptive.

text: Decay changes the optimisation trajectory. Train and validation loss histories differ from the unregularized arm at every seed, even though test predictions are identical.
limitations: Derived from the experiment summary, not a registered endpoint. The size of the difference depends on the single fixed learning rate and budget.

text: Reproducibility audits pass. Accuracy recomputed from stored predictions matches every record, and an independent from-scratch retrain reproduces all arm records on checkpoint hash, predictions, example IDs, accuracy and loss history.
limitations: Post-hoc audit run after the registered comparison, so it is exploratory by the protocol rules. Reproduction was checked on this machine and CUDA build only.

text: The checkpoint norm comparison differs from the hypothetical repeated pure-decay multiplier. The fitted arms also follow different gradient trajectories, so their norm ratio is not a measurement of isolated decay. This descriptive comparison does not establish why test predictions coincide or identify a mechanism for the accuracy result.
limitations: Derived after the results were known, from one checkpoint per arm per seed. The predicted shrink follows from the update rule and the constants, but the measured shrink is not a clean single-variable intervention. The discrepancy is recorded, not resolved.

text: The sensitivity audit tabulates normal-approximation calculations under assumed discordance rates. These are planning scenarios, not an empirical detection threshold. Observed agreement does not establish the population discordance rate, equivalence, or a hard lower bound on detectable effects.
limitations: The calculation assumes a discordance rate and a normal approximation. It is not a power analysis for every alternative or for the correlated multi-seed estimator, and it does not establish that smaller effects must be inconclusive.

text: The saved post-hoc negative-log-likelihood analysis reports higher loss with decay and a conditional interval excluding zero. This is a distinct exploratory endpoint. It does not test the registered accuracy hypothesis, and other continuous measurements, including validation loss, also changed.
limitations: Not a registered endpoint and chosen after the primary result was known, so it cannot be promoted to confirmatory. The bootstrap is conditional on the trained models. Three of three seeds with the same sign has two-sided sign-test p = 0.25, so consistency across seeds is weak evidence. A pre-registered continuous endpoint in a new cycle is needed.

text: Implementation checks pass: study.py check reproduces the registered split sizes, and the 13-test pytest suite passes. The decoupled-decay step is covered by a zero-gradient test.
limitations: The checks cover the properties tested, not the full training loop. The shuffled-label permutation is checked only through C2.

text: Code audit: the fixture's reload check and prediction step run eval-mode forward passes on all 1797 feature rows, which include the 360 test features (the pilot's code path does this too, although the pilot reports validation metrics only). No test label was found in the training or model-selection paths that were read.
limitations: Found by reading the code, not by a runtime leakage test. Disclosed in reports/pilot.md. Not fixed in this cycle, because study.py is the immutable fixture. Read-only audit, so 'no label found' is not proof of absence.

text: Other registered prediction checks pass on arms that study.py labels exploratory. P4: pilot validation accuracy and the logistic and real-label MLP test accuracies lie in the registered ranges. P5: shuffled-label test accuracy is near chance, within the registered 0.05-0.16 range and below the 0.20 failure threshold. P6: class-prior test accuracy equals the majority-class fraction of the test split exactly. A4(d): accuracy recomputed from stored predictions matches the records.
limitations: The predictions were registered, but these arms are labelled exploratory by the fixture, so the outcomes are reported under that label. The shuffled arm uses the same decay as the regularized arm, so P5 does not isolate decay. Accuracy near chance cannot detect every label-permutation bug. The class-prior and logistic results come from one seed each.
